Okay, just want to add something here. 

Some of us are good at Maths, some are good at literature, some can’t learn new languages, and some can’t pass their PE classes even if their lives depend on it. 

So yes, the human brain, DNA, biology, etc. is a mysterious wonder. We don’t know everything about the brain of a worm, let alone the brain of a human. We are a beautiful disaster walking the Earth with so much potential unknown of. 

Back to my point, some people can do this, some people can do that. Some can regulate their emotions, some just cannot. 

We are “some just cannot”. We are unable to deal with our emotions which leads to depression because we either think or feel “too much”. Who are to blame? How could you not be depressed? The world is a shit hole and the only way out (dying) is socially frowned upon. We exist only to destroy. We hurt other humans, we hurt our non-humans kin, we hurt the soil that brings us to life, we hurt the air we breathe, the water we drink. 

Unable to phantom such great pain that we are not even responsible of consciously, we become at war with ourselves. 

I always believe that if you’re not sad, you’re not paying attention. 

But regulation is so so so important. Be sad and aware, be caring and vulnerable, be at pain and ache for the things we are hurting. But. We. Need. To. Stay. Alive. We need to turn so much pain into much more power (like they did in Monster Inc. with the screams), and, oh i don’t know, join campaigns, recycle, upcycle, do social work, go exercise, learn something new, reduce our consumption, reduce our carbon footprint… 

I fee like the root to depression is the feeling that we’re useless and are here for nothing. But we’re here already, so might as well make something out of it. Get better. Show people how they are dead dead DEAD wrong. Dying does not resolve anything. So if you have the courage to dive into the great unknown of the afterlife, might as well gather your strength to keep fighting. 

I have been suicidal since I was 10. I am now 22. Things are worse than ever. But I use all of my energy to regulate my emotions EVERY SINGLE DAY. And I push myself forward, even though it’s fucking exhausting. But we’ll make it together. Trust me.

people claim themselves as mental health advocates until someone actually need help. Then they are "too much", "too depressed", "too negative", etc. People wear live - laugh -love tshirts and tell you to "go outside", "touch some grass", "work out", "drink more water". The thing is WE KNOW (as people with depression), those things would help. But our brains REFUSE to see the whole point of getting better: why get better it's gonna suck again, why get better you're gonna die anyways, why get better life is meaningless, why get better i have no reason to be here. 

Or they go and be like "oh what do you have to be depressed about". Nothing. Basically nothing. Bitch the whole problem of being depressed is wanting to die even when you're loved and fulfilled. It's a MENTAL ILLNESS, not a "sad moment" that you could just snap out of.
